title: Intraday Market Overview
intro:
US Stocks End Lower as Treasury Yields Hit 5% and Oil Surges Ahead of Fed Decision🔥

U.S. stocks closed lower on Tuesday as investors grappled with the highest Treasury yields in nearly two decades, a sharp rally in oil prices driven by Middle East supply disruptions, and growing anticipation ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision.
The S&P 500 fell 0.45% to 7,585.73, extending its recent weakness with a sixth decline in the past seven sessions. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.63% to 52,093.11, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.78% to 25,981.57. The Russell 2000 declined 0.8% as investors reduced risk exposure ahead of Wednesday’s FOMC announcement.

Bond Market and Federal Reserve
Market sentiment remained dominated by the bond market after the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly climbed to 5.041%, its highest level since 2007, before easing slightly to close near 5.01%.
The move reflects growing concerns that rising energy prices and persistent inflationary pressures could force policymakers to maintain a restrictive stance for longer than previously expected. Investors are currently pricing in roughly a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase at Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting.

Energy Sector Leads the Market
Energy was the strongest-performing sector of the session as crude oil prices continued to surge.

Brent crude traded near $109 per barrel while WTI crude climbed more than 4% to settle at $105.53 after Saudi Arabia suspended operations on its critical East-West pipeline, a major route used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
The oil rally boosted energy stocks across the board. APA Corporation, Valero Energy, Marathon Petroleum, Devon Energy, and Phillips 66 all posted strong gains as investors increased exposure to companies expected to benefit from higher crude prices.
Overall, the Energy sector advanced 2.26%, making it the best-performing group within the S&P 500.

Technology Sector Remains Under Pressure
Technology shares remained under pressure as rising Treasury yields continued to weigh on growth valuations.
However, semiconductor stocks partially recovered from Monday’s AI-driven selloff. Qualcomm gained roughly 4%, while Advanced Micro Devices rose 2.3%. Nvidia, Intel, and Micron Technology also traded higher as investors selectively returned to chipmakers following the previous session’s sharp decline.
Despite the rebound, sentiment toward the broader AI sector remains cautious as markets continue to evaluate the long-term implications of growing discussions surrounding AI safety and regulation.

Communication Services Outperform
The Communication Services sector gained more than 2.8%, continuing its recent outperformance and helping offset weakness elsewhere in the market.
At the same time, eight of the eleven major S&P 500 sectors finished in negative territory. Both Technology and Consumer Discretionary declined roughly 1.7%, while Industrials also weakened amid concerns that elevated borrowing costs could slow economic activity.

Financials Struggle
Financial stocks came under pressure as bond market volatility intensified.
Goldman Sachs fell approximately 1.2%, leading losses within the Dow Jones Industrial Average as investors assessed the impact of higher yields and ongoing uncertainty surrounding investment banking activity.

Corporate Movers
Among notable individual movers, Enova International plunged 23.4% after withdrawing proposed acquisition applications related to Grasshopper Bancorp, citing regulatory uncertainty.
Meanwhile, Dave & Buster’s moved lower after reporting quarterly revenue that missed analyst expectations, raising concerns about consumer spending trends.

Cryptocurrency Sector Weakens
Cryptocurrency-related assets faced renewed pressure after the U.S. Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, a major crypto market structure bill.
The setback left uncertainty surrounding the future regulatory framework for digital assets in the United States. Bitcoin retreated toward the $75,000 level, while Coinbase Global shares also came under pressure.

Commodities and Currency Markets
In precious metals, gold recovered above $4,300 per ounce after two consecutive declines as the recent surge in Treasury yields and oil prices temporarily lost momentum ahead of major central bank decisions.
The U.S. Dollar Index strengthened toward 99.7, approaching its highest level in a month as traders positioned for the Federal Reserve announcement.
Oil prices eased slightly during Asian trading after API data showed a surprise increase of 7.14 million barrels in U.S. crude inventories. Nevertheless, ongoing supply disruptions in Saudi Arabia and operational challenges in Libya continue to support the broader bullish outlook for energy markets.

International Markets
In Asia, Japan provided another indication that AI-related demand remains strong despite recent volatility in technology shares.
Japanese exports rose 19.3% year-over-year in August, exceeding expectations and supported by strong demand for semiconductors and AI-related components. However, core machinery orders declined more than expected, highlighting continued uncertainty surrounding business investment.

Outlook
All eyes are now on the Federal Reserve.
While a quarter-point rate increase appears largely priced in, investors will focus on the updated economic projections, the revised dot plot, and comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh for clues regarding the path of monetary policy through the remainder of the year.
With Treasury yields at their highest levels since 2007, crude oil near multi-month highs, inflation concerns re-emerging, and risk assets facing increasing pressure, the Federal Reserve’s message could determine market direction for the rest of September.

Market Focus Today: Federal Reserve rate decision, updated economic projections, dot plot forecasts, Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference, crude oil inventory data, Treasury yield movements, and the U.S. dollar reaction.
